chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Abi Abdullah, from his father, from Harun ibn al-Jahm, from Ja'far ibn Umar, from Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him), who said:
The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) forbade men from entering upon women except with their permission.
ai.seo_question: What is the Islamic ruling on men entering upon women without permission?
ai.summary: Recorded in al-Kafi, this hadith from Imam al-Sadiq (AS) underscores the Prophetic precedent for respecting female privacy, a principle deeply rooted in Shia jurisprudence regarding mahram and non-mahram interactions. It serves as a foundational text for the legal requirement of permission (idhn) before entering a woman's private space, emphasizing both modesty and mutual respect within the domestic sphere. This ruling is often cited by scholars to derive broader etiquette (adab) for family life and social conduct.
